diagnosis:
All four rollouts settled cleanly (no turn-cap auto-fails), all four facts were revealed in every rollout, and all provenance checks (P1–P4) passed every time. The failures are entirely on content checks C7, C8, C9, and C10 — and in every failing case the fact was revealed, cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement's decision value was correct. This points to ENCODING MISMATCH on the *commitment* sub-requirements of these checks.

Rollout 0 (C7, C8, C9 false): PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4 all revealed and cited. Settlement decisions all correct (3M/1.8M/monthly/30 days/500K). The commitments use type "document_upload" for all four agents. C7 (gates PF1's Elias commitment), C8 (gates PF2's Mei commitment), and C9 (gates PF3's Jonas commitment) all failed. The passing rollout 1 used type "documentation" for these same commitments and all checks passed. This strongly indicates C7/C8/C9 expect a commitment type string that the model only sometimes produces — rollout 0's "document_upload" was rejected while rollout 1's "documentation" was accepted, yet both describe the same underlying commitment.

Rollout 2 (C7, C9, C10 false): PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4 all revealed and cited; decisions all correct. Commitment types here are "document_receipt" (Ruth), "document_upload" (Elias), "document_circulation" (Jonas), "checklist_update" (Mei). C7 (Elias, PF1) failed — same "document_upload" type as rollout 0. C9 (Jonas, PF3) failed — type was "document_circulation" here but "document_upload" in rollout 0; the only rollout where C9 passed (rollout 1) used type "documentation". C10 (Ruth, PF4) failed — type was "document_receipt" here; the passing rollout 1 used "documentation". This confirms the pattern: these checks accept a narrow commitment-type vocabulary (likely just "documentation") but reject semantically-equivalent alternates the model naturally produces.

Rollout 3 (C7, C8, C9 false; C10 true): PF1–PF4 all revealed and cited; decisions all correct. All four commitments use type "document_upload". C7 (Elias/PF1), C8 (Mei/PF2), C9 (Jonas/PF3) all failed with "document_upload"; C10 (Ruth/PF4) passed with "document_upload". This is the critical contradiction: in rollout 0, Ruth's commitment with type "document_upload" had C10=true; in rollout 3, Ruth's commitment with the same type "document_upload" also had C10=true. But C7/C8/C9 failed on "document_upload" in both rollouts 0 and 3. So C7/C8/C9 reject "document_upload" while C10 accepts it — the checks have inconsistent type requirements for the same commitment category, and the model cannot predict which type each individual check wants.

Summary of per-check failure modes across rollouts:
- C7 (PF1, Elias commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH in rollouts 0, 2, 3. The Elias commitment was always present with the correct target and detail, but the type field was "document_upload" (rollouts 0, 3) or "document_upload" (rollout 2) — rejected by C7. Only rollout 1 passed C7 with type "documentation".
- C8 (PF2, Mei commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH in rollouts 0, 3. Mei's commitment was present with correct detail but type "document_upload" — rejected. Rollout 1 passed with "documentation"; rollout 2 passed with "checklist_update". So C8 accepts "documentation" and "checklist_update" but rejects "document_upload".
- C9 (PF3, Jonas commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH in rollouts 0, 2, 3. Jonas's commitment was present with correct detail but type was "document_upload" (rollouts 0, 3) or "document_circulation" (rollout 2) — both rejected. Only rollout 1 passed with type "documentation".
- C10 (PF4, Ruth commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH in rollout 2 only. Ruth's commitment was present with correct detail but type "document_receipt" — rejected. Rollout 1 passed with "documentation"; rollouts 0 and 3 passed with "document_upload". So C10 accepts "documentation" and "document_upload" but rejects "document_receipt".

The root cause is that C7, C8, C9, and C10 each gate on a specific commitment-type string but the model produces a variety of semantically-valid type labels ("document_upload", "document_circulation", "document_receipt", "checklist_update", "documentation") depending on the natural wording of each agent's documentation commitment. The checks are too narrow to accept the natural variation. This is not a disclosure problem (all facts were always revealed), not a telepathy problem (facts were always cited), not a misapplied problem (decisions were always correct), and not a pacing problem (no turn-cap failures).

C7.why: The draft requests $5,000,000 and specifies no reserve; PF1 changes maximum_bank_exposure_usd to exactly $3,000,000, loss_reserve_usd to exactly $1,800,000, and requires Elias's exposure-and-reserve documentation commitment.

C9.why: The draft has no termination right; PF3 changes termination_notice_days to exactly 30 and requires Jonas's redline-circulation or document commitment.

C10.why: The requested exposure has no documented credit support and would not support approval on the draft terms; PF4 changes parent_guarantee_usd to exactly $500,000 and makes conditional approval feasible with Ruth's guarantee-documentation commitment.

C8.why: The draft has no AML review frequency; PF2 changes enhanced_aml_review_frequency to exactly monthly and requires Mei's checklist-update commitment.
